contributions.item_title_en: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
contributions.text_english:
A high number of schools across my constituency of Caerdydd Ffynnon Taf are facing a maintenance backlog. Scaffolding has surrounded Roath Park primary since 2021, Marlborough Road primary since 2022 and Albany primary since 2023. The condition of a number of comprehensives is substandard and very close to being further downgraded, including the second-hand Welsh-medium comprehensives ysgol Bro Edern and ysgol Plasmawr.

Most worryingly, parents at Albany Primary School were advised the week before this term started that their children would be sent out to three different schools because of dry rot. This late notice was despite Estyn warning in October 2025 that the site management arrangements at Albany Primary School, and I quote,

'give cause for concern and have been brought to the attention of the local authority.'

What discussions has the Cabinet Minister had with Cardiff Council regarding the condition of their school estate, and the council's response to Estyn in particular, and whether earlier intervention could have avoided Albany primary's closure and the severe disruption caused to pupils' education?

contributions.item_title_en: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
contributions.text_english: Thank you, Minister, for your statement today.
contributions.text_original: Diolch, Weinidog, am eich datganiad heddiw.

contributions.item_title_en: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
contributions.text_english: I appreciate the update and that this Government is taking this work seriously to better support impacted residents. For years now, residents have been afraid in their own homes and have felt that this issue has not been given the attention it deserves. Despite receiving assurances that their property was safe when they moved in, one resident in Cardiff has shared that they face a £3,000 cost for a waking watch, which costs £15,000 a week between 96 flats, and the management company are having to find £150,000 to install fire-detecting equipment. Without the necessary improvements, residents have faced the possibility of being made homeless as their homes aren't safe to live in. I welcome the Minister introducing financial support as an interim measure while remediation works are carried out. How will the Minister make sure tenants don't have to pay out of pocket for remediation work again? Diolch.

contributions.item_title_en: 4. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Finance: Rebalancing the non-domestic rates system
contributions.text_english:
As we know, high streets are at the heart of our communities, and the Cabinet Minister's announcement today to cut business rates by 30 per cent for hospitality and leisure businesses across Wales is a very welcome step to rebalance the non-domestic rate system. In addition to today's announcement, can you confirm whether any consideration has also been given to the small business rates relief threshold and, as Sam has already mentioned and you've touched upon, business rates holidays for new businesses, both of which would be a boost for our local entrepreneurs?

Whilst there would be a cost to such measures, one way to cover this, perhaps, would be to consider different valuation methods or multipliers for certain types of property, for example, data centres, which do not currently have their own classification. This way, some of the extractive profit generated from these properties could be retained and instead used to benefit local communities.

I look forward to working with the Cabinet Minister on longer term reforms that fall outside today's scope of this announcement.

contributions.item_title_en: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
contributions.text_english: Diolch, Weinidog, for your commitment to championing a community-centred planning system and strengthening the voice of local people. Cymru is emerging as a significant location for data-centre development, with two designated UK Government AI growth zones. However, they have no dedicated use class and no mention in 'Planning Policy Wales', even though their scale and energy and water demands raise important questions for our environment and our planning system beyond their immediate locality. As you know, in my own constituency of Caerdydd Ffynnon Taf, a data centre is proposed in Llanrumney, replacing the Cardiff east park and ride, which serves the University Hospital of Wales, and this has given rise to a controversy beyond the immediate locality. The proposed 150 MW facility, only a short distance from primary schools and local homes, will rely on fossil-fuelled gas turbines as well as polluting standby diesel generators. Will the Minister, therefore, set out what plans the Government has to review the planning requirements for data centres, and in particular look into the Cardiff east park-and-ride application, so that communities like Llanrumney don't end up paying the social and environmental price while the profit goes elsewhere? Diolch.

contributions.item_title_en: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
contributions.text_english:
For nearly 50 years, successive UK Governments, Conservative and Labour, have followed Margaret Thatcher's broken neoliberal ideology that puts profit before people. Our national utilities have been sold off at a fraction of their value, and tens of billions of pounds of dividends have been extracted. The French Government now owns our nuclear power industry. A Czech billionaire owns the Royal Mail. Here in Cymru, our heavy industry and the communities it supported have been abandoned, while Westminster is spending £100 billion on HS2 for half a railway that costs more than NASA's mission to the moon.

Then there are the scandals: PFI, PPE, the sale of MOD homes, not to mention an illegal war in Iraq, 20 wasted years in Afghanistan, and now complicity in Israel's genocide in Gaza. So, on the contrary, Cabinet Minister, what assessment is being made into the benefit to Wales of not being part of the United Kingdom? Diolch.

contributions.text_english: As a new Member, the most sobering meeting I had in my first week was with the Senedd's security team—perhaps like many others here—and to hear their advice on dealing with potential threats in the future and the possible impact on our families, who, after all, didn't choose to be elected. Language is important and words have consequences. Things said in here do have the potential to have a wider impact outside. Given the increase in contributions in the Siambr over recent weeks that some might find inflammatory, can the Commission confirm whether these have been associated with heightened safety concerns for Members or a need to improve security in this seventh Senedd?

contributions.item_title_en: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
contributions.text_english: Diolch. One in two people in Wales will be diagnosed with cancer at some point in their lives, and this is something that affects us all. Therefore, the proposal of our new Government to develop a 10-year cancer plan is both well overdue and very welcome. One area often overlooked and highlighted to me by a constituent is metastatic breast cancer and incurable stage 4 cancer in general. In particular, there is no data on how many people are living with metastatic cancer in Wales, even though collection of this data became mandatory over 12 years ago. Without clear information on diagnosis, recurrence, treatment pathways and outcomes, we can't identify variations between health boards or ensure that every patient receives timely, equitable support. Please can the Minister prioritise the consistent implementation of the metastatic breast cancer pathway signed off by the Wales cancer network in 2023 and ensure that metastatic cancer is not overlooked in the new national cancer plan? Diolch.

contributions.item_title_en: 3. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Priorities for Local Government, Housing and Planning
contributions.text_english: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Private renters are under growing pressure, with rents in Wales rising faster than anywhere else in the UK, up nearly 9 per cent in the past year, and even higher in parts of Cardiff. Rent is expected to be around 30 per cent of income, yet only 42 per cent of tenants in Wales now consider it affordable, a figure that has continued to fall each year. At the same time, protections under the previous Government have been among the weakest in the UK, and, as we have heard, Wales remains the only nation still permitting no-fault evictions with no cap on rent bidding. Therefore, I'd like to ask the Cabinet Minister for assurance that progress is under way to strengthen protections for renters and explain how rent reforms will be implemented across Wales. Diolch.
